subject: SecureAssess: Evidence request — ephemeral CI credentials & deploy gating
messages:
From: Kristen Miller <kristen.miller@secureassess.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: SecureAssess SOC Team <soc-team@secureassess.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — ephemeral CI credentials & deploy gating

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of the SIG/SOC2 evidence collection for our customer assessment, we need artifacts that demonstrate your "ephemeral credentials and CI/CD gating" controls. Specifically we are asking for: 

- IAM policy for CI runners / ephemeral service accounts (JSON)
- Rotation logs for short-lived keys or tokens covering the last 90 days (or a redacted sample)
- CI pipeline config showing deploy gates / PR-required checks (screenshots or YAML)
- Runbook or playbook describing how you revoke or rotate compromised runner tokens
- Evidence that secrets are never printed to logs (pipeline logs with redactions)

Please let us know whether you can provide the originals or need to sanitize anything. Our deadline to close these items is Friday, 19 Jun 2026. Preferred delivery is a shared Drive folder with a short manifest file.

If any of these items need to be handled by your security/infrastructure teams, feel free to copy them in.

Best regards,
Kristen Miller
Senior Assessor, SecureAssess LLC
kristen.miller@secureassess.com

--
SecureAssess: SIG/SOC2 evidence intake
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Evidence request — ephemeral CI credentials & deploy gating

Kristen — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a package and upload it to a Drive folder (link below). A couple quick clarifying Qs so we scope what to drop into the folder: 

1) For rotation logs, do you need full originals (with usernames/timestamps) or a redacted CSV sample is OK? We can provide both if necessary, but full logs include internal service-account IDs.
2) For the CI pipeline screenshots: are high-level workflow YAML + one canary deploy screenshot sufficient, or do you require live runner audit trails?

Planned deliverables (tentative):
- ci-runner-iam-policy.json (our runner role and least-privilege statements)
- ephemeral-key-rotation-log-2026Q2.csv (redacted service-account ids, full timestamps)
- deploy-gate-runbook-2026-06.pdf (runbook for gating and emergency rollback)
- sample-pipeline-config.yml (GitHub Actions) + PR-gating screenshots
- manifest.txt describing redactions and mapping to SIG controls

Marcus and Mina, can you confirm we can share the attached policy and rotation CSV by EOD Monday (15 Jun)? Marcus: can you add the pipeline screenshots? Mina: please attach the runbook draft.

Drive folder (will set permissions to allow SecureAssess view): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bxx/CI-credentials

Thanks — we'll get this over quickly.

— Dylan

Dylan / Kristen — quick update and answers to Dylan's questions.

1) Rotation logs: we will provide a redacted CSV for Q2 that preserves timestamps and rotation event types but replaces internal service-account IDs with deterministic tokens (svc-01, svc-02). If SecureAssess needs originals under an NDA, we can coordinate offline.

2) Pipeline artifacts: we will include the GitHub Actions workflow YAML for our deploy pipeline and a screenshot of the PR merge gating in the console (required checks + protection rules). Runner audit trails are available but contain ephemeral session tokens; we can provide a trimmed audit with only event types and timestamps.

Mechanism summary (short):
- Runners authenticate via OIDC to our cloud provider, acquiring short-lived role credentials (max lifetime 4 hours).
- Secrets are issued by Vault (HashiCorp) using dynamic secrets for DB creds and are injected at runtime; we never persist raw secrets in repo or runner images.
- CI/CD deploys are gated by required status checks, code-owner approvals for prod branches, and a manual approval step for canary-to-prod rollout.

Attachments uploaded to Drive folder (read-only link above):
- ci-runner-iam-policy.json (attached)
- ephemeral-key-rotation-log-2026Q2.csv (attached, redacted)
- deploy-gate-runbook-2026-06.pdf (attached)
- sample-pipeline-config.yml (attached)

Marcus, please confirm the IAM policy and pipeline screenshots match what I attached.

Thanks,
Mina
Engineering Manager — Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Hi all — thanks, this is helpful. I can confirm receipt of the Drive folder and the three attachments listed below. A couple follow-ups before we close the control: 

- Can you add one example of a canary rollout approval (screenshot showing the manual approval step and the audit event)? That helps us validate the human gating control for production.
- For the rotation CSV, please include one row showing a rotation event plus the revocation action (you can redact principal details).

If you can drop those two items into the same folder by Friday 19 Jun, we should be able to mark the control as evidence-complete. Also please include a short manifest.txt inside the folder describing which SIG control IDs each file maps to (e.g., SIG-CC-06: ephemeral credentials).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Kristen
